tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Browser.close should stop the browser process when the close command fails
reason: Stubs Puppeteer's own BiDi connection so its `browser.close` command rejects, then checks that the browser process exits anyway. Strider has no connection to stub: its scope closes the browser (asking it to close, then signals), and an in-process rejection of a close command is not a Strider call to make. Puppeteer runs this on Firefox's BiDi only; Strider's Firefox close path is covered by the launch tests that close browsers

tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.launch should return the default arguments
[launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.launch should report the correct lastLaunchedBrowser
reason: Asks Puppeteer which flags its launch would pass (`puppeteer.defaultArgs`) and which browser it last launched (`puppeteer.lastLaunchedBrowser`): its own bookkeeping, with Puppeteer's flag names. Strider's flags are the inspectable LaunchProfile values a launch records, and nothing is computed from the options without launching

tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.launch should not allow setting debuggingPort and pipe
reason: Checks that Puppeteer refuses a debugging port and a pipe together. Strider has neither option (its transport is its own, and a debugging port is an argument), so the refusal has no counterpart

tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.executablePath should work
[launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.executablePath returns executablePath for channel
[launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.executablePath when executable path is configured its value is used
reason: Puppeteer's own executable resolution: finding the browser it downloaded or its channel, and its configured path. Strider never looks up or downloads a browser (method-browsertype-executablepath is different), so there's no resolution of Puppeteer's to test

tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.launch userDataDir argument
reason: Passes the profile directory as a Chromium or Firefox flag (`--user-data-dir`, `-profile`). Stock WebKit's MiniBrowser has no profile flag: its profile is the `userDataDir` option, which the userDataDir tests cover

tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.launch userDataDir argument with non-existent dir
reason: Passes the profile directory as a Chromium or Firefox flag (`--user-data-dir`, `-profile`) for a directory that doesn't exist yet. Stock WebKit's MiniBrowser has no profile flag, as the userDataDir argument test says

tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.launch tmp profile should be cleaned up
reason: Redirects where the temporary profile is created (Puppeteer's `temporaryDirectory` configuration) and checks it's removed after close. Strider has no option for the temporary profile's location, and a launch doesn't report its profile's path. The nearest matrix row is the artifacts directory, which is a different set of files

tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.launch should filter out ignored default arguments in Chrome
[launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.launch should filter out ignored default argument in Firefox
reason: Drops named default arguments from a launch (`ignoreDefaultArgs`) and reads the process's spawn arguments back. Strider has no such option, and its profile's arguments are a value the caller builds; a launch doesn't expose its process's arguments either

tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.launch should set the default viewport
reason: A launch-wide default viewport (`defaultViewport`) for every page the browser opens. Strider's viewport is declared per page or context, and the nearest matrix row is the per-page one; the launch-wide default isn't there

tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.launch should support the AbortSignal
reason: Stops a launch with an `AbortSignal` (`signal`) and waits for the process to exit. Strider has no signal option: cancelling a launch is interruption of the effect that builds it. The process's exit can't be observed from the browser either. The nearest matrix row is launch itself

tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.connect should support targetFilter option in puppeteer.launch
reason: Filters the launch's targets (`targetFilter`, with `waitForInitialPage: false`) and reads the browser's targets back. Strider has no launch-time target filter and no target list; the nearest matrix row is a context's pages, which aren't filtered at launch

tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.connect should support targetFilter option
reason: Filters the targets a connection sees (`targetFilter`) by URL. Strider's connection observes every page of the browser, with no filter; the nearest matrix row is a context's pages

tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.connect should be able to close remote browser
[launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.connect should be able to connect to a browser with no page targets
reason: Closes a browser the client connected to (`remoteBrowser.close()`), which ends the browser for every client and emits `disconnected`. Strider's connection is an attached browser: its scope ends the connection, and the browser stays open. The nearest matrix row is the launched browser's close, which the layer owns

tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Puppeteer Puppeteer.connect should support acceptInsecureCerts option
reason: Connects with `acceptInsecureCerts` and reads the response's security details (the TLS protocol, which must match the server's socket). Strider has no connect-level option for certificates (its `acceptInsecureCerts` is a context option, unsupported on Chromium), and NetworkResponse has no security details

tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Browser target events should work
reason: Subscribes to browser-level `targetcreated`, `targetchanged`, and `targetdestroyed` events and checks the sequence of URLs. Strider has no browser-level target events, and its pages are a watchable list with no URL-change stream; the nearest matrix row is the context's page events

tests: [launcher.test] Launcher specs Browser.Events.disconnected should be emitted when: browser gets closed, disconnected or underlying websocket gets closed
reason: Counts the browser's `disconnected` events across clients, the host, and a closed socket. Strider has no browser-level disconnected event: each connection's end is its scope's, and the browser's close is observed on its context's `closed`

reason: Connects a client to the running browser (`puppeteer.connect`), or reads the endpoint it listens on. Strider's stock WebKit layer has no connect; Chromium and Firefox connect with their own layers, so these run there
